summary: Both editions were reviewed independently against all clauses of the supplied Greek working source. Both preserve the commands, speakers, rod conditions, negations, comparisons, and group assignments. The standard edition’s bracketed occurrences of “rods” transparently supply the noun understood in the Greek; the simplified edition makes such implicit referents explicit without changing the assertions. The contextual descriptions of eaten rods and the linen garment are defensible renderings, not concrete fidelity defects. No alternative readings or manuscript reports were supplied for disclosure review. Acceptance is limited to fidelity to this working source and project policy, not authentication of manuscripts, exhaustive collation, or scholarly certification.
